doctrine: This document is a curated scrape of Adobe Creative Cloud learning resources and tutorials. Core content centers on Lightroom Classic and Lightroom on the web: organizing/importing photos (Library module), editing techniques (exposure, clarity, saturation, white balance, color grading), selective editing with masks and brushes, removing distractions (dust, lens spots, background objects, reflections), special workflows (panorama merging, silhouettes, portrait enhancement, underwater correction, landscape photography, perspective correction). Also includes one substantial Adobe-authored piece on the Creative Strategy Framework by Douglas Davis (4-column method: target audience + facts + features/benefits + message/objective) as strategic foundation for creative work. The framework emphasizes discovering novel connections across data to produce unexpected insights versus standard executions. Heavy repetition of 'Quick Actions' and dust removal tutorials suggests incomplete or redundant scraping. Mostly instructional UI/procedural content; minimal strategic, positioning, or business methodology.
workflows: Library module: import, organize, create collections, sync across devices
Develop module: apply auto tone, adjust exposure/tone/clarity/saturation, color grade
Selective editing: use Brush tool with Auto Mask, create masks via AI or manual selection
Panorama merge: select overlapping shots, choose projection method, use Boundary Warp to preserve edges
Portrait enhancement: darken eyebrows, sharpen eyelashes, brighten irises, lighten eye whites, deepen lip color
Landscape masking: use AI to detect sky/mountains/water/vegetation, create separate masks for adjustments
Distraction removal: dust (visualize, apply AI, customize per image), people/reflections (AI detection + removal)
Upright/perspective correction: use Auto presets or Guided Upright with manual guides on horizontal/vertical lines
Assisted Culling: sort by subject focus/eye focus/exposure, auto-reject documents/overexposed, organize into flags/ratings/albums
Cross-device sync: edits sync cloud-native across Lightroom desktop/mobile/web via Adobe ID
Generative Upscale: enlarge cropped/low-res images 2x or 4x using Topaz Gigapixel model, apply at end of edit workflow
prompts: Creative Strategy Framework: (1) What is the target's problem and how to align it with a solution? (2) What internal/external data exists about the brand/product? (3) Which features map to customer benefits? (4) What single message should the customer take away?

Photo editing checklist: Auto tone first, then adjust Exposure/Highlights/Shadows/Blacks, add Clarity/Vibrance, color balance with White Balance eyedropper or Temp/Tint sliders, apply masking for selective edits
tools: Lightroom Classic (Library, Develop, Print, Book, Map modules)
Lightroom on the web (browser-based editing with masking, Quick Actions)
Lightroom mobile (iOS/Android sync, in-app camera capture)
Adobe Photoshop (linked editing: Edit In workflow, Healing/Spot Healing)
Photoshop Fix (healing/spot healing for quick touch-ups)
Adobe Spark Post (template-based ad creation from Lightroom photos)
Topaz Gigapixel AI model (upscaling integrated into Lightroom)
Creative Cloud Libraries (asset sync across apps)
operating_rules: Always start with Auto tone button for instant exposure/color corrections
Use masking before global adjustments for precise control
Apply Generative Upscale at end of editing workflow, not mid-edit
Enable Lens Corrections and Remove Chromatic Aberration in Optics panel before perspective work
Dust removal should occur before creating masks to avoid mask update cascades
Use Boundary Warp in panorama merge to preserve full image without cropping detail
For portrait retouching: isolate eyebrows/lashes/iris with tight brush sizes (1.6-2.9), use Feather to soften edges, increase Flow/Density for quick application
Color Variance slider: move left to reduce color range (fix uneven skies, blotchy skin), move right to enhance color differences
Quick Actions analyze image content and suggest one-click edits; available in Lightroom on web and Lightroom mobile
Assisted Culling operates in Library module and Import window; allows AI-based focus/exposure/composition scoring with rejection presets
